user.t: why am i getting this in my ruflo console ✗ initialise ruflo in this project (.claude-flow, .claude settings and the mods):

resp.t:
That ✗ doesn't mean anything is broken. The init action never ran because the confirmation timed out.

The console's last result says: **"the confirm came more than 30 s after the ask; ask again"**. Actions that change files show a Yes/No prompt and expire after 30 seconds. You answered after that, so it was discarded.

**Separate issue: typing `/ruflo init` won't work.** `/ruflo <word>` only opens views like `hive`, `swarm` or `settings`. Init is a palette entry inside the console, labelled **"init ruflo here"**.

**To retry:** open the console with `/ruflo`, choose **"init ruflo here"**, and press `y` within 30 seconds.

**Check where you are first.** The console is running in `C:\Users\mariu`, your home folder, not a project. That folder already has a `.claude-flow` folder and a `.claude\settings.json`, so it has been set up here at least partly before. Also, `.claude\settings.json` in your home folder is your global Claude Code settings file, so running init here would edit settings that apply to every project. You probably want to start Claude Code inside the actual project folder and run init there.

**There's also a prompt waiting now:** "start a hive-mind (raft)", from opening the Hive-Mind view. If you didn't mean to start one, press `n` or let it expire. Don't start a hive until init has run in the right folder.

If you tell me which project folder you want, I can run init for you. I'll need you to give me permission to run console actions, because right now I'm set to read-only.

resp.t:
The main thing this board shows is that you're still in your home folder, not a project. The status line reads `ruflo: C:\Users\mariu`, and there's no mission goal yet ("✎ goal: use the palette"). Setting things up in the right place matters more than anything else on the menu right now.

1. **Open Claude Code in a real project folder.** Exit, `cd` into the repo you want to work on, and start Claude Code there. Everything ruflo creates (`.claude-flow`, settings, swarm and hive state) goes into whichever folder you're in. Right now that's your home folder, where `.claude\settings.json` is your global settings file.
2. **Initialise ruflo there.** Press `p` for the Command Palette, run **"init ruflo here"**, and press `y` within 30 seconds. Your last try failed only because the confirmation timed out.
3. **Set a goal.** Press `1` for Missions and type what you're building, for example "add a dark mode toggle". The board then follows its research → create → build → test → validate → secure → benchmark → learn steps toward that goal.
4. **Check its health.** Press `u` for Security & Doctor to confirm the setup worked.

Leave Hive-Mind, Swarm, Federation and Self-Evolution alone for now. They only help once a goal is running, and starting them early is how you got the leftover "start a hive-mind" prompt. Also keep an eye on Cost & Budget: it already shows $1.85 spent.

If you tell me which project folder to use, I can do steps 2–4 for you. I'm read-only in the console right now, so you'd need to let me run actions first.

user.t: what project folder are we currently in

resp.t:
You're not in a project folder. This session is running in **`C:\Users\mariu`**, your Windows home folder, which isn't a git repository. The ruflo console's status line shows the same path (`ruflo: C:\Users\mariu`).

To work on a project, quit Claude Code, `cd` into the project's folder (for example `cd C:\Users\mariu\code\my-app`), and run `claude` from there. The console will then show that path, and "init ruflo here" will set ruflo up for that project instead of your home folder.

If you're not sure where your projects are, I can list the folders in your home directory that look like code projects.
